title: Thyroid hormone therapy in a population cohort over two decades indicates persistent overtreatment
authors: Zwanziger D, Kowall B, Klose JM, Schmidt B, Stang A, Führer D
population: Participants of the German population-based Heinz Nixdorf Recall (HNR) cohort, examined in 2000 to 2003 (n = 3561, mean age 59.4 years), 2006 to 2008 (n = 3933) and 2011 to 2015 (n = 3048, mean age 68.7 years), and of its multigenerational study of children and partners, examined in 2013 to 2016 (n = 2741, mean age 53.8 years) and 2020 to 2023 (n = 1610); each visit analysed cross-sectionally
funder: DF and DZ report funding by DFG (SFB/TR 296 LOCOTACT, Project-ID 424957847) for data analysis. All other authors declare that no funds were received for the manuscript.
authorConflicts: The authors declare no financial interests.
result: In the HNR cohort, thyroid hormone use was 9.3% (329 of 3561; 9.2% in the abstract) in 2000 to 2003, 12.5% (491) in 2006 to 2008 and 15.3% (465 of 3048) in 2011 to 2015, while self-reported thyroid disease was 22.8%, 25.2% and 28.8%; the abstract describes thyroid disease as stable. Median TSH was lower in treated participants, most of all in older individuals. Among thyroid hormone users, TSH was below 0.45 mIU/l in 35% (114 of 329), 25% (124 of 491) and 24% (112 of 465) at the three HNR visits, and in 24% (81 of 339) and 12% (24 of 197) at the two multigenerational visits (Table 4, Table 5 and results text). The abstract instead describes the 35% and 25% as the proportion of participants with TSH below 0.45 mIU/l who took thyroid hormone, which the tables contradict.
